Kilowallet 1.0.0 (30) — RC7

This build fixes the iOS Lightning bridge behind the “no such LND call: routerSendPaymentV2” error. The fix also applies to calls for opening, closing and resizing channels, tracking payments and receiving invoices.

Settings → BTC node & explorer now lets you scan or enter your own Knots (BLAKE2b) node. With this option on, the node receives watch-only public descriptors and can link your wallet’s addresses and history. Your recovery words and spending keys stay on the phone. The RPC login is stored in the iOS Keychain. For HTTPS, compare the certificate fingerprint on your node before trusting it. Onion connections use the built-in Tor. Kilojoin and JoinBlaket continue to use Electrum.

Test with an empty or synthetic wallet. Update in place; keep your current wallet installed. Check that switching wallets and reopening the app preserves receive addresses, frozen/reserved coins, pending activity, and wallet-specific Ark and Lightning state. To try the RPC screen, use an isolated test node. Do not send real funds, open or close real channels, or include recovery words, RPC passwords or backup files in feedback.

The publisher verified automated migration tests, native simulator tests, and the iPhone Release build. Live payments and physical-device node connectivity have not been verified for this build.
